newsitem.title: HUNGARY: GERMANY'S SPUETZ AG SETS UP HUNGARY UNIT.
newsitem.headline: GERMANY'S SPUETZ AG SETS UP HUNGARY UNIT.

text.p: Germany's leading interdealer fixed income broker Spuetz AG has set up Hungary's first interdealer broker, Bondtrade Ertekpapir Rt, company officials said on Wednesday.

Bondtrade will mediate between banks and brokerages on the secondary market of goverment papers in order to secure a better flow of information and thus higher liquidity, Bondtrade's director Karoly Misky told a news conference.
"One advantage is that the less active market participants will be continuously informed about the actual market situation," Misky said.
"The other advantage is that deals can be concluded more quickly," he said, adding that a further benefit will be the anonymous way of dealing.
He added that Bondtrade will not do business on its own account.
Misky said that Bondtrade's mediation will cover all government papers and in the future may add corporate papers and derivative products.

Bondtrade, 95 percent owned by Spuetz AG and five percent owned by Hungary's Capital Penzugyi es Tanacsado Rt, was launched with 20 million forints capital and is expected to become operational within two weeks, Misky said.

In Hungary, the Government Debt Management Agency (AKK) organises the country's new government securities issues and has launched a primary dealer system for securities houses, with 22 participating currently, to make the secondary market of government papers more transparent.
